findings_qualitative.value: LVC consistent with swept-up gas in jet-driven bow shock; HVC decelerating jet/entrained material

evidence.quote: we conclude that the LVC in IRAS 16342$-$3814 corresponds to material of the CSE that has been swept-up by the jet-driven bow shock.

claims.hypothesis: Peak-position PV structure arises from real velocity gradients in a narrow outflow, not a wide-angle constant-speed outflow
claims.experiment: SHAPE model with HVC and LVC power-law velocity fields compared with CO(3-2) PV
claims.finding: Collimated decelerating HVC inside accelerating LVC

evidence.quote: our model circumvents the problem of assuming a constant expansion velocity

claims.experiment: Mass spectrum power laws and morphology

evidence.quote: This double power-law variation of the mass with velocity is exactly what observations have revealed in other molecular outflows

claims.hypothesis: The HVC peak positions trace a precessing jet
claims.finding: Small-angle precession compatible with IR corkscrew

evidence.quote: Given the limited angular and spectral resolution of these observations, it is difficult to discern which rotation angle gives the best fit.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Sahai et al. 2017 constant-velocity wide-angle (~90 deg) model rejected

evidence.quote: The constant expansion velocity assumption is most likely not true

limitations_admitted.value: Mass and slopes are lower limits if CO(3-2) optically thick

evidence.quote: if the CO($J$=3$\rightarrow$2) line is optically thick, the values of these power-law exponents represent just a lower limit

referee_caveats_inferred: Model fit by eye with no uncertainties or degeneracy exploration
Precession parameters depend strongly on the arbitrary rotation angle
Unresolved HVC width and peak-position scatter limit the sinusoid
